The **Axiom of Choice** (AC) is the following statement.

> Every family of nonempty sets has a choice function
> ([[def-choice-function]]).

Written out: for every set $\mathcal{F}$ all of whose members are nonempty,
there exists a function $g$ with domain $\mathcal{F}$ satisfying $g(S) \in S$ for
all $S \in \mathcal{F}$.

An equivalent formulation is that a product of nonempty sets is nonempty: if
$X_i \ne \emptyset$ for every $i \in I$, then $\prod_{i \in I} X_i \ne \emptyset$.
Here $\prod_{i \in I} X_i$ is the set of functions $f$ with domain $I$ such that
$f(i) \in X_i$ for every $i \in I$; when a family of nonempty sets is indexed by
itself, such an $f$ is precisely a choice function for it.

The **Axiom of Countable Choice**, written $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, is the following
statement.

> For every family $(X_n)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ of nonempty sets indexed by
> $\mathbb{N}$ there is a function $f$ with domain $\mathbb{N}$ such that
> $f(n) \in X_n$ for every $n \in \mathbb{N}$.

Equivalently, in the vocabulary of [[def-choice-function]]: every at most
countable family of nonempty sets ([[def-countable]]) has a choice function.

Assume Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $\Omega\subseteq\mathbb R^n$ be open and bounded in one direction: there are a unit vector $e$ and $a<b$ with $a<x\cdot e<b$ for every $x\in\Omega$. Let $1\le p<\infty$. Then $\|u\|_{L^p(\Omega)}\le C(p)\,(b-a)\,\|Du\|_{L^p(\Omega)}$ for every $u\in W^{1,p}_0(\Omega;\mathbb K)$.

Assume Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $H$ be a real or complex Hilbert space, let $a$ be a bounded coercive sesquilinear form on $H$ with constants $M,\alpha$ ([[def-bounded-coercive-and-symmetric-sesquilinear-forms]]), and let $F:H\to\mathbb K$ be a bounded conjugate-linear functional with norm $\|F\|=\sup_{\|v\|\le1}|F(v)|$. Then there is a unique $u\in H$ with $$a(u,v)=F(v)\qquad\text{for every }v\in H,$$ and it satisfies $\alpha\|u\|\le\|F\|$, that is $\|u\|\le\|F\|/\alpha$. The real bilinear case is the same statement with $a$ symmetric or not, $F$ a bounded linear functional, and the conjugation read as the identity.

Assume Countable Choice. Let $\Omega\subseteq\mathbb R^n$ be open, $n\ge1$, and $\mathbb K\in\{\mathbb R,\mathbb C\}$. On $H^1(\Omega)=W^{1,2}(\Omega;\mathbb K)$ ([[def-sobolev-space-wkp-and-its-norm]], [[def-hk-and-hk-zero-notation]]) define $$(u,v)_{H^1}:=(u,v)_{L^2}+\sum_{i=1}^n(D_iu,D_iv)_{L^2},$$ with the $L^2$ inner product of [[lem-l-two-with-the-integral-pairing-is-a-hilbert-space]]. Then $(\cdot,\cdot)_{H^1}$ is an inner product on the Sobolev classes whose induced norm is the $W^{1,2}$ norm of [[def-sobolev-space-wkp-and-its-norm]], and $H^1(\Omega)$ is a Hilbert space for it. The zero-boundary space $H^1_0(\Omega)$ is a closed subspace of $H^1(\Omega)$ ([[def-wkp-zero-as-a-sobolev-closure]]) and hence a Hilbert space for the restricted inner product. The pairing is linear in the first argument and conjugate-linear in the second, in the convention of [[def-real-and-complex-inner-product-space]].

A **real Hilbert space** is a real inner-product space $H$ ([[def-real-and-complex-inner-product-space]]) whose induced-length metric is complete in the sense of [[def-complete-metric-space]]: every Cauchy sequence in $H$ for the norm $\|v\|=\sqrt{\langle v,v\rangle}$ ([[cor-inner-product-induces-a-norm]]) converges to a point of $H$. A **complex Hilbert space** is a complex inner-product space with the same completeness property, so that a Hilbert space is exactly a real or complex inner-product space that is a Banach space for its induced norm ([[def-banach-space]]).

**The completion convention is the Cauchy-sequence one.**
[[def-banach-space]] defines completeness by convergence of Cauchy sequences, and this page keeps that convention throughout. It is weaker than $\sigma$-completeness — the assertion that every decreasing sequence of nonempty closed subsets with diameters tending to zero has a nonempty intersection. The two agree in ZFC, but Blackadar, Farah and Karagila note that the closest-point theorem on a $\sigma$-complete inner-product space is provable in ZF, whereas the Cauchy-complete form used below consumes the Axiom of Countable Choice; nothing here silently imports the stronger notion.

Assume Countable Choice. Let $\Omega\subseteq\mathbb R^n$ be open with
$n\ge1$, let $k\in\mathbb N_0$, let $1\le p\le\infty$, and let
$\mathbb K\in\{\mathbb R,\mathbb C\}$.

Every $\varphi\in C_c^\infty(\Omega;\mathbb K)$ belongs to
$W^{k,p}(\Omega;\mathbb K)$. Indeed $\varphi$ is bounded with compact support,
hence lies in $L^p(\Omega;\mathbb K)$ for every exponent in range, and each of
its classical partial derivatives is again smooth and compactly supported,
hence lies in $L^p(\Omega;\mathbb K)$ and is the corresponding weak derivative
by [[lem-classical-derivatives-are-weak-derivatives]].

Define the **zero-boundary Sobolev space**
$$W_0^{k,p}(\Omega;\mathbb K):=\overline{C_c^\infty(\Omega;\mathbb K)},$$
the closure taken in the normed space
$(W^{k,p}(\Omega;\mathbb K),\|\cdot\|_{W^{k,p}(\Omega)})$ of
[[def-sobolev-space-wkp-and-its-norm]]. The norm is a genuine norm on classes
by [[lem-sobolev-norm-is-well-defined-and-definite]], so this is the usual
metric closure of a subset of a normed space: $u\in W_0^{k,p}(\Omega;\mathbb K)$
if and only if for every $\delta>0$ there is
$\varphi\in C_c^\infty(\Omega;\mathbb K)$ with
$\|u-\varphi\|_{W^{k,p}(\Omega)}<\delta$. Write
$H_0^k(\Omega):=W_0^{k,2}(\Omega;\mathbb K)$ when the scalar field is fixed by
context.

Three warnings are part of the definition. First, this is a closure of
almost-everywhere classes, and all its equalities are equalities of Sobolev
classes. Second, no pointwise boundary values and no trace characterization
are asserted: a description of $W_0^{k,p}$ by vanishing boundary data belongs
to the later trace theory and is not used here. Third, the closure is defined
for every $1\le p\le\infty$, but for $p=\infty$ it is not claimed that every
compactly supported $W^{k,\infty}(\Omega)$ function lies in $W_0^{k,\infty}(\Omega)$;
the definition merely names the closure of the test functions.

statement.

> For every family $(X_n)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ of nonempty sets indexed by
> $\mathbb{N}$ there is a function $f$ with domain $\mathbb{N}$ such that
> $f(n) \in X_n$ for every $n \in \mathbb{N}$.

Equivalently, in the vocabulary of [[def-choice-function]]: every at most
countable family of nonempty sets ([[def-countable]]) has a choice function.

Assume Countable Choice. For every $1\le p<\infty$ there is
$C_{d,p}<\infty$ such that for all
$u\in W^{1,p}(\widehat S_d;\mathbb R)$,
$$\|u-u_{\widehat S_d}\|_{L^p(\widehat S_d)} \le C_{d,p}|u|_{W^{1,p}(\widehat S_d)},\qquad u_{\widehat S_d}:=|\widehat S_d|^{-1}\int_{\widehat S_d}u\,dx.$$

Assume Countable Choice. Let $1<p<\infty$ and $p'=p/(p-1)$. For each facet $F$ of
$\widehat S_d$, restriction of smooth functions extends uniquely to a
bounded linear trace map
$$\gamma_F:W^{1,p}(\widehat S_d;\mathbb R)\to L^p(F;\mathbb R).$$
For real-valued $u\in W^{1,p}(\widehat S_d)$ and
$G\in W^{1,p'}(\widehat S_d;\mathbb R^d)$, the facet traces satisfy
$$\int_{\widehat S_d}u\,\operatorname{div}G+\nabla u\cdot G\,dx =\sum_{F\subset\partial\widehat S_d}\int_F\gamma_Fu\,\gamma_FG\cdot\widehat n_F\,dS.$$
Here $\gamma_FG$ is the componentwise trace and $\widehat n_F$ is the
outward unit normal. The bounded C1-domain trace and Green theorems are not
used for the simplex.

Assume Countable Choice. Let $F_K(\widehat x)=b_K+A_K\widehat x$ map the fixed reference simplex
$\widehat S_d$ bijectively to a cell $K$ of a shape-regular family, and let
$h_K$ be its diameter and $\rho_K$ its inradius. There are constants
$c,C>0$, depending only on $d$, the reference simplex, and the shape
regularity bound, such that
$$c h_K\le s_{\min}(A_K)\le \|A_K\|\le C h_K, \qquad c h_K^d\le\det A_K\le C h_K^d.$$
For each facet $F$, its affine surface Jacobian is comparable to
$h_K^{d-1}$, and its altitude from the opposite vertex is comparable to

The **Axiom of Countable Choice**, written $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, is the following
statement.

> For every family $(X_n)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ of nonempty sets indexed by
> $\mathbb{N}$ there is a function $f$ with domain $\mathbb{N}$ such that
> $f(n) \in X_n$ for every $n \in \mathbb{N}$.

Equivalently, in the vocabulary of [[def-choice-function]]: every at most
countable family of nonempty sets ([[def-countable]]) has a choice function.

Let $V$ be a vector space over $\mathbb K\in\{\mathbb R,\mathbb C\}$, let
$V_h\subseteq V$ be a subspace, let $a$ be linear in its first argument and
conjugate-linear in its second, and let $F:V\to\mathbb K$ be conjugate-linear.
If $u\in V$ and $u_h\in V_h$ satisfy
$$a(u,v)=F(v)\quad(v\in V),\qquad a(u_h,v_h)=F(v_h)\quad(v_h\in V_h),$$
then
$$a(u-u_h,v_h)=0\qquad\text{for every }v_h\in V_h.$$

by [[lem-classical-derivatives-are-weak-derivatives]].

$$W_0^{k,p}(\Omega;\mathbb K):=\overline{C_c^\infty(\Omega;\mathbb K)},$$

$(W^{k,p}(\Omega;\mathbb K),\|\cdot\|_{W^{k,p}(\Omega)})$ of

by [[lem-sobolev-norm-is-well-defined-and-definite]], so this is the usual
metric closure of a subset of a normed space: $u\in W_0^{k,p}(\Omega;\mathbb K)$
if and only if for every $\delta>0$ there is
$\varphi\in C_c^\infty(\Omega;\mathbb K)$ with
$\|u-\varphi\|_{W^{k,p}(\Omega)}<\delta$. Write
$H_0^k(\Omega):=W_0^{k,2}(\Omega;\mathbb K)$ when the scalar field is fixed by
context.

Three warnings are part of the definition. First, this is a closure of
almost-everywhere classes, and all its equalities are equalities of Sobolev
classes. Second, no pointwise boundary values and no trace characterization
are asserted: a description of $W_0^{k,p}$ by vanishing boundary data belongs
to the later trace theory and is not used here. Third, the closure is defined
for every $1\le p\le\infty$, but for $p=\infty$ it is not claimed that every
compactly supported $W^{k,\infty}(\Omega)$ function lies in $W_0^{k,\infty}(\Omega)$;

Assume Countable Choice. Let $\Omega\subseteq\mathbb R^n$ be open with
$n\ge1$, $k\in\mathbb N_0$, $1\le p\le\infty$, and
$\mathbb K\in\{\mathbb R,\mathbb C\}$. Write
$$\mathcal A_k=\{\alpha\in\mathbb N_0^n:|\alpha|\le k\}.$$
This is a finite nonempty set: every coordinate of such an $\alpha$ lies in
$\{0,\ldots,k\}$, and it contains the zero multi-index.

The real and complex $L^p$ classes use the conventions in
[[def-l-p-space-as-a-quotient-by-null-functions]] and
[[def-complex-lp-and-euclidean-test-function-conventions]]. Their quotient
norm values are supplied by
[[thm-the-l-p-norm-descends-to-the-quotient-and-makes-l-p-a-normed-space]]
for real scalars and
[[thm-complex-holder-minkowski-and-the-quotient-norm]] for complex scalars.

Define $W^{k,p}(\Omega;\mathbb K)$ to be the set of classes
$u\in L^p(\Omega;\mathbb K)$ such that, for every $\alpha\in\mathcal A_k$,
there is an $L^p(\Omega;\mathbb K)$ class with a locally integrable
representative $v_\alpha$ satisfying
$$\int_\Omega u\,D^\alpha\varphi\,dx =(-1)^{|\alpha|}\int_\Omega v_\alpha\varphi\,dx \qquad\text{for every }\varphi\in C_c^\infty(\Omega).$$
Here the weak derivative is the one in
[[def-weak-derivative-of-a-locally-integrable-function]]. Under
[[def-countable-choice]], local integrability of $L^p$ representatives and
invariance under null-set changes follow from
[[lem-weak-derivative-is-independent-of-lp-representatives]], while
[[lem-weak-derivatives-are-unique-almost-everywhere]] gives uniqueness of each
locally integrable derivative class. Thus this condition is a condition on the
$L^p$ class $u$, and each resulting derivative determines one $L^p$ class,
denoted $D^\alpha u$. The test pairing is bilinear, without conjugation.

$$W^{0,p}(\Omega;\mathbb K)=L^p(\Omega;\mathbb K).$$
The Sobolev norm expression is
$$\|u\|_{W^{k,p}(\Omega)}= \begin{cases} \left(\displaystyle\sum_{\alpha\in\mathcal A_k} \|D^\alpha u\|_{L^p(\Omega)}^p\right)^{1/p},&1\le p<\infty,\\[1ex] \displaystyle\max_{\alpha\in\mathcal A_k} \|D^\alpha u\|_{L^\infty(\Omega)},&p=\infty. \end{cases}$$

A compatible labeled initial mesh is a finite matching affine simplicial triangulation $\mathcal T_0$ of a polygon in $\mathbb R^2$ as in [[def-matching-affine-simplicial-meshes]]; matching means distinct cell interiors are disjoint and any shared boundary is a complete common facet. with labels on its edges such that each triangle has one edge labeled $0$ and two labeled $1$, and every shared edge has the same label from both incident triangles. For a descendant triangle of generation $g(K)$, its three edge labels, in any order, are $(g(K)+1,g(K)+1,g(K))$. The unique edge labeled $g(K)$ is its reference edge.

To bisect $K$, join the midpoint of its reference edge to the opposite vertex. The two resulting triangles have generation $g(K)+1$. In each child, the two new half-edges and the bisector receive label $g(K)+2$; the one inherited nonreference edge retains label $g(K)+1$ and is the child's reference edge. A finite bisection forest is the collection of the initial triangles and all descendants reached by finitely many such bisections; its leaves form a triangulation when all shared-edge subdivisions agree. The admissible family $\mathbb T(\mathcal T_0)$ consists of the matching conforming leaf triangulations generated by these compatible bisections. A refinement $\mathcal T\le\mathcal T_*$ means every cell of $\mathcal T_*$ lies in a cell of $\mathcal T$.

The compatible initial labeling is a hypothesis, not a consequence of an arbitrary initial triangulation. This definition is two-dimensional and makes no claim about three-dimensional closure or complexity.

The **Axiom of Countable Choice**, written $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, is the following
statement.

> For every family $(X_n)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ of nonempty sets indexed by
> $\mathbb{N}$ there is a function $f$ with domain $\mathbb{N}$ such that
> $f(n) \in X_n$ for every $n \in \mathbb{N}$.

Equivalently, in the vocabulary of [[def-choice-function]]: every at most
countable family of nonempty sets ([[def-countable]]) has a choice function.

Assume Countable Choice. Let $1<p<\infty$ and $p'=p/(p-1)$. For each facet $F$ of
$\widehat S_d$, restriction of smooth functions extends uniquely to a
bounded linear trace map
$$\gamma_F:W^{1,p}(\widehat S_d;\mathbb R)\to L^p(F;\mathbb R).$$
For real-valued $u\in W^{1,p}(\widehat S_d)$ and
$G\in W^{1,p'}(\widehat S_d;\mathbb R^d)$, the facet traces satisfy
$$\int_{\widehat S_d}u\,\operatorname{div}G+\nabla u\cdot G\,dx =\sum_{F\subset\partial\widehat S_d}\int_F\gamma_Fu\,\gamma_FG\cdot\widehat n_F\,dS.$$
Here $\gamma_FG$ is the componentwise trace and $\widehat n_F$ is the
outward unit normal. The bounded C1-domain trace and Green theorems are not
used for the simplex.

Orient every top-dimensional cell of a matching simplicial mesh by the
ambient orientation of $\mathbb R^d$, and orient each facet by the induced
boundary convention of [[def-oriented-simplicial-cell-chains]]. In the sum
of the oriented boundaries of all top-dimensional cells, every interior
facet occurs twice with opposite signs; every boundary facet occurs once.

Assume Countable Choice. Let $\Omega\subseteq\mathbb R^n$ be open with
$n\ge1$, let $k\in\mathbb N_0$, let $1\le p\le\infty$, and let
$\mathbb K\in\{\mathbb R,\mathbb C\}$.

Every $\varphi\in C_c^\infty(\Omega;\mathbb K)$ belongs to
$W^{k,p}(\Omega;\mathbb K)$. Indeed $\varphi$ is bounded with compact support,
hence lies in $L^p(\Omega;\mathbb K)$ for every exponent in range, and each of
its classical partial derivatives is again smooth and compactly supported,
hence lies in $L^p(\Omega;\mathbb K)$ and is the corresponding weak derivative
by [[lem-classical-derivatives-are-weak-derivatives]].

Define the **zero-boundary Sobolev space**
$$W_0^{k,p}(\Omega;\mathbb K):=\overline{C_c^\infty(\Omega;\mathbb K)},$$
the closure taken in the normed space
$(W^{k,p}(\Omega;\mathbb K),\|\cdot\|_{W^{k,p}(\Omega)})$ of
[[def-sobolev-space-wkp-and-its-norm]]. The norm is a genuine norm on classes
by [[lem-sobolev-norm-is-well-defined-and-definite]], so this is the usual
metric closure of a subset of a normed space: $u\in W_0^{k,p}(\Omega;\mathbb K)$
if and only if for every $\delta>0$ there is
$\varphi\in C_c^\infty(\Omega;\mathbb K)$ with
$\|u-\varphi\|_{W^{k,p}(\Omega)}<\delta$. Write
$H_0^k(\Omega):=W_0^{k,2}(\Omega;\mathbb K)$ when the scalar field is fixed by
context.

Three warnings are part of the definition. First, this is a closure of
almost-everywhere classes, and all its equalities are equalities of Sobolev
classes. Second, no pointwise boundary values and no trace characterization
are asserted: a description of $W_0^{k,p}$ by vanishing boundary data belongs
to the later trace theory and is not used here. Third, the closure is defined
for every $1\le p\le\infty$, but for $p=\infty$ it is not claimed that every
compactly supported $W^{k,\infty}(\Omega)$ function lies in $W_0^{k,\infty}(\Omega)$;
the definition merely names the closure of the test functions.

Assume Countable Choice. Let $\mathcal T$ be a finite matching affine simplicial mesh of a bounded
polyhedral open set $\Omega$, let $1\le p\le\infty$, and let $v$ be a
real-valued scalar member of the conforming piecewise-polynomial space in
[[def-broken-and-conforming-polynomial-spaces]]. Then $v\in W^{1,p}(\Omega)$.
Its weak gradient agrees almost everywhere on each cell with the ordinary
cellwise polynomial gradient.

Assume Countable Choice. Let $\Omega$ be a bounded polyhedral open set with a finite matching
affine simplicial mesh, let $1\le p<\infty$, and let $v$ be a real-valued
conforming piecewise polynomial whose polynomial trace vanishes on every boundary
facet. Then
$$v\in W^{1,p}_0(\Omega),\qquad \|v\|_{L^p(\Omega)}\le C_\Omega\|\nabla v\|_{L^p(\Omega)}.$$
Here $W^{1,p}_0$ is the norm closure of $C_c^\infty(\Omega)$; no C1
trace characterization is used.

Fix a finite conforming triangular mesh $\mathcal T$. For each interior vertex $z$, choose the incident triangle with least fixed mesh index and denote it $K_z$. On the reference triangle $\widehat K$, let $\widehat\lambda_1,\widehat\lambda_2,\widehat\lambda_3$ be its barycentric coordinates. The Gram matrix $G_{ij}=\int_{\widehat K}\widehat\lambda_i\widehat\lambda_j$ is positive definite because $\int_{\widehat K}p^2>0$ for every nonzero $p\in P_1(\widehat K)$. Thus there are unique dual affine polynomials $\widehat\psi_i\in P_1(\widehat K)$ with $\int_{\widehat K}\widehat\lambda_j\widehat\psi_i=\delta_{ij}$. Pull them to $K_z$ by the affine map using the normalized measure so $\int_{K_z}\varphi_y\psi_{z,K_z}=\delta_{zy}$ for its three local nodal hats.

For $v\in H_0^1(\Omega)$ set $c_z(v)=\int_{K_z}v\psi_{z,K_z}$ at interior vertices and $c_z(v)=0$ at boundary vertices. Define
$$I_{\mathcal T}v=\sum_{z\ {\rm interior}}c_z(v)\varphi_z,$$
where $\varphi_z$ is the continuous piecewise-affine nodal hat. The sum is finite and belongs to the conforming zero-boundary P1 space. This is a moment quasi-interpolant; it is not a point-evaluation operator on arbitrary Sobolev classes.

$$|v|_{W^{\ell,p}(\widehat S_d)} \le C|v|_{W^{m,q}(\widehat S_d)}\qquad(v\in\widehat P).$$

Its boundary nodal coefficients are zero, so [F2] places it in $V(\mathcal T)$. If $v\in V(\mathcal T)$, then on the selected cell $K_z$ its affine restriction is a linear combination of the three local hats. The dual moment identities recover its nodal coefficient at $z$, so $c_z(v)=v(z)$ at every interior vertex; at boundary vertices both the coefficient and the P1 trace value are zero. Therefore $I_{\mathcal T}v=v$.

For a cell $K$ not meeting the boundary, set $c=v_{\omega_K}$; for a boundary cell set $c=0$. The patch Poincaré estimate gives $\|v-c\|_{L^2(\omega_K)}\le Ch_K\|\nabla v\|_{L^2(\omega_K)}$. For each interior vertex $z$ of $K$, put $a_z=c_z(v)-c=\int_{K_z}(v-c)\psi_{z,K_z}$; this equality follows from the dual identities, which give $\int_{K_z}\psi_{z,K_z}=1$. These are local integrals of an $L^2(K_z)$ function, with no application of $I_{\mathcal T}$ to $v-c$. The scaled dual bound gives $|a_z|\le Ch_K^{-1}\|v-c\|_{L^2(K_z)}$, since $K_z\subset\omega_K$ and its diameter is comparable to $h_K$. At a boundary vertex of $K$, necessarily $c=0$ and the corresponding coefficient difference is zero. The three barycentric hats on $K$ sum to one, so $(I_{\mathcal T}v-c)|_K=\sum_{z\in\mathcal V(K),\ z\ {\rm interior}}a_z\varphi_z|_K$. Each hat has $L^2(K)$ norm at most $Ch_K$ and gradient norm at most $C$. This argument uses only that each selected $K_z$ is incident to $z$, so its constants are uniform over all such selections.

A compatible labeled initial mesh is a finite matching affine simplicial triangulation $\mathcal T_0$ of a polygon in $\mathbb R^2$ as in [[def-matching-affine-simplicial-meshes]]; matching means distinct cell interiors are disjoint and any shared boundary is a complete common facet. with labels on its edges such that each triangle has one edge labeled $0$ and two labeled $1$, and every shared edge has the same label from both incident triangles. For a descendant triangle of generation $g(K)$, its three edge labels, in any order, are $(g(K)+1,g(K)+1,g(K))$. The unique edge labeled $g(K)$ is its reference edge.

To bisect $K$, join the midpoint of its reference edge to the opposite vertex. The two resulting triangles have generation $g(K)+1$. In each child, the two new half-edges and the bisector receive label $g(K)+2$; the one inherited nonreference edge retains label $g(K)+1$ and is the child's reference edge. A finite bisection forest is the collection of the initial triangles and all descendants reached by finitely many such bisections; its leaves form a triangulation when all shared-edge subdivisions agree. The admissible family $\mathbb T(\mathcal T_0)$ consists of the matching conforming leaf triangulations generated by these compatible bisections. A refinement $\mathcal T\le\mathcal T_*$ means every cell of $\mathcal T_*$ lies in a cell of $\mathcal T$.

The compatible initial labeling is a hypothesis, not a consequence of an arbitrary initial triangulation. This definition is two-dimensional and makes no claim about three-dimensional closure or complexity.

For any compatible 2D initial labeling from [[def-afem-nvb-labelled-triangulation-family]], every conforming NVB descendant has shape regularity bounded by a constant depending only on the initial mesh. Three complete generations of uniform bisection of a triangle split each original edge at its midpoint, create a new interior midpoint on the median from the opposite vertex, and give child diameters at most half the parent diameter.

Their node union $F=F_1\cup F_2$ is a forest: every nonroot node keeps its parent, and a node is either a leaf in both forests or has its same two children in at least one; if it has children in either forest, the union contains both. The common initial edges have equal labels. Induct on the bisection depth of any shared edge: its midpoint is uniquely determined by the segment, and its two half-edge labels are determined by the same generation rule [F1]; therefore both incident forests prescribe the same descendants on that edge. The leaves of $F$ consequently form a matching conforming triangulation refining both $\mathcal T_1$ and $\mathcal T_2$. For a descendant triangle of generation $g(K)$, its three edge labels, in any order, are $(g(K)+1,g(K)+1,g(K))$. The unique edge labeled $g(K)$ is its reference edge.

To bisect $K$, join the midpoint of its reference edge to the opposite vertex. The two resulting triangles have generation $g(K)+1$. In each child, the two new half-edges and the bisector receive label $g(K)+2$; the one inherited nonreference edge retains label $g(K)+1$ and is the child's reference edge. A finite bisection forest is the collection of the initial triangles and all descendants reached by finitely many such bisections; its leaves form a triangulation when all shared-edge subdivisions agree. The admissible family $\mathbb T(\mathcal T_0)$ consists of the matching conforming leaf triangulations generated by these compatible bisections. A refinement $\mathcal T\le\mathcal T_*$ means every cell of $\mathcal T_*$ lies in a cell of $\mathcal T$.

The generation is a nonnegative integer, so after finitely many strict drops the chain reaches the boundary or a compatible pair. To refine $K$, recursively refine this chain from its terminal end back to $K$. A terminal boundary cell is bisected first; a terminal compatible pair is bisected simultaneously. Inductively, the next cell in the chain has its reference edge on the edge just bisected, so that midpoint is already present on the other side when it is split. Thus every split matches its neighbor and conformity is preserved.

Let $g(K)$ denote generation. Each bisection halves area, and [F2] gives constants $c_0,C_0>0$ depending only on the finitely many initial shapes such that $c_0\,2^{-g(K)}\le |K|\le C_0\,2^{-g(K)}$ and $\operatorname{diam}K\le C_0\,2^{-g(K)/2}$. Fix $T^*\in\mathcal M$ with generation $g^*$. At a fixed generation $g\le g^*+1$, cells with nonzero allocation lie in a ball of radius $D B2^{-g/2}$ about $T^*$. Each has area at least $c_0 2^{-g}$ by step 2.1, while that ball enlarged by one cell diameter has area at most $C_D2^{-g}$. If the parent was created during closure, take the least-ID requested cell whose recursive chain created it; repeat this at each earlier creation time. This gives a finite sequence of requested cells $T_1,\ldots,T_J$ ending at an initial cell. The **Axiom of Countable Choice**, written $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, is the following
statement.

> For every family $(X_n)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ of nonempty sets indexed by
> $\mathbb{N}$ there is a function $f$ with domain $\mathbb{N}$ such that
> $f(n) \in X_n$ for every $n \in \mathbb{N}$.

Equivalently, in the vocabulary of [[def-choice-function]]: every at most
countable family of nonempty sets ([[def-countable]]) has a choice function.

Assume Countable Choice, as in the Sobolev and simplex trace suppliers.

Let $\mathcal T$ be a matching triangular mesh, $U\in V(\mathcal T)$, and $u$ solve the weak model from [[def-afem-p1-residual-estimator-and-data-oscillation]]. For every $v\in H_0^1(\Omega)$,
$$\int_\Omega\nabla(u-U)\cdot\nabla v+(b\cdot\nabla(u-U))v =\sum_{K\in\mathcal T}\int_K R_K(U)v-\sum_{E\ {\rm interior}}\int_EJ_E(U)v.$$

Assume Countable Choice, as in the Sobolev, affine-scaling and trace suppliers.

Let $\mathcal T$ be a shape-regular conforming triangular mesh and let $I_{\mathcal T}$ be the moment interpolant from [[def-afem-local-moment-interpolant]]. For each cell $K$, let $\omega_K$ be the union of vertex stars of its vertices. There is a constant $C$ depending only on shape regularity such that for every $v\in H_0^1(\Omega)$,
$$\|v-I_{\mathcal T}v\|_{L^2(K)}\le Ch_K\|\nabla v\|_{L^2(\omega_K)},\quad \|\nabla I_{\mathcal T}v\|_{L^2(K)}\le C\|\nabla v\|_{L^2(\omega_K)},$$
and, for every interior edge $E\subset\partial K$,
$$\|v-I_{\mathcal T}v\|_{L^2(E)}\le Ch_E^{1/2}\|\nabla v\|_{L^2(\omega_K\cup\omega_{K'})},$$
where $K'$ is the other incident cell. The operator maps into $V(\mathcal T)$ and reproduces every member of $V(\mathcal T)$.

Assume Countable Choice. Fix polynomial degree $k\ge0$, $1\le p,q\le\infty$, and integers
$0\le m\le\ell\le k$. Let the shape-regular affine simplex family be as in
[[def-matching-affine-simplicial-meshes]]. For every cell $K$ in that family,
there is a constant independent of cell size such that, for every
$v\in\mathbb P_k(K)$ and every facet $F\subset\partial K$,
$$|v|_{W^{\ell,p}(K)} \le C h_K^{m-\ell+d(1/p-1/q)}|v|_{W^{m,q}(K)},$$
$$\|v\|_{L^p(F)} \le C h_K^{(d-1)/p-d/q}\|v\|_{L^q(K)}.$$
Use $1/\infty=0$. Constants may depend on $d,k,p,q$ and the family shape
regularity bound, but not on $K$ or $h_K$.

Assume Countable Choice. Let $F_K(\widehat x)=b_K+A_K\widehat x$ map the fixed reference simplex
$\widehat S_d$ bijectively to a cell $K$ of a shape-regular family, and let
$h_K$ be its diameter and $\rho_K$ its inradius. There are constants
$c,C>0$, depending only on $d$, the reference simplex, and the shape
regularity bound, such that
$$c h_K\le s_{\min}(A_K)\le \|A_K\|\le C h_K, \qquad c h_K^d\le\det A_K\le C h_K^d.$$
For each facet $F$, its affine surface Jacobian is comparable to
$h_K^{d-1}$, and its altitude from the opposite vertex is comparable to
$h_K$. Thus Sobolev scaling constants can be expressed using $h_K$ alone,
with constants uniform over the family.

For any compatible 2D initial labeling from [[def-afem-nvb-labelled-triangulation-family]], every conforming NVB descendant has shape regularity bounded by a constant depending only on the initial mesh. Three complete generations of uniform bisection of a triangle split each original edge at its midpoint, create a new interior midpoint on the median from the opposite vertex, and give child diameters at most half the parent diameter.

Assume Countable Choice. Let $\mathcal T$ be a finite matching affine simplicial mesh of a bounded
polyhedral open set $\Omega$, let $1\le p\le\infty$, and let $v$ be a
real-valued scalar member of the conforming piecewise-polynomial space in
[[def-broken-and-conforming-polynomial-spaces]]. Then $v\in W^{1,p}(\Omega)$.
Its weak gradient agrees almost everywhere on each cell with the ordinary
cellwise polynomial gradient.

Assume Countable Choice. Let $\Omega$ be a bounded polyhedral open set with a finite matching
affine simplicial mesh, let $1\le p<\infty$, and let $v$ be a real-valued
conforming piecewise polynomial whose polynomial trace vanishes on every boundary
facet. Then
$$v\in W^{1,p}_0(\Omega),\qquad \|v\|_{L^p(\Omega)}\le C_\Omega\|\nabla v\|_{L^p(\Omega)}.$$
Here $W^{1,p}_0$ is the norm closure of $C_c^\infty(\Omega)$; no C1
trace characterization is used.

The **Axiom of Countable Choice**, written $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, is the following
statement.

> For every family $(X_n)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ of nonempty sets indexed by
> $\mathbb{N}$ there is a function $f$ with domain $\mathbb{N}$ such that
> $f(n) \in X_n$ for every $n \in \mathbb{N}$.

Equivalently, in the vocabulary of [[def-choice-function]]: every at most
countable family of nonempty sets ([[def-countable]]) has a choice function.

Assume Countable Choice for the $L^2$ and Sobolev conventions of [[def-countable-choice]].

All functions and data are real-valued. Let $\Omega\subset\mathbb R^2$ be a bounded polygon and let $\mathcal T$ be a finite conforming matching triangulation by nondegenerate affine triangles, with maximum shape-regularity constant $\Gamma$. Write $h_K=\operatorname{diam}K$ and $h_E=\operatorname{diam}E$. Let $V(\mathcal T)$ be the continuous, piecewise-affine zero-boundary subspace of [[def-broken-and-conforming-polynomial-spaces]], which lies in $H_0^1(\Omega;\mathbb R)$ by [[thm-matching-continuous-piecewise-polynomials-are-wkp]] and [[thm-zero-boundary-piecewise-polynomials-in-w10p]]. The exact weak model is
$$-\Delta u+b\cdot\nabla u=f,\qquad u\in H_0^1(\Omega;\mathbb R),\quad f\in L^2(\Omega;\mathbb R),\quad b\in\mathbb R^2\ \text{constant}.$$
The weak form is $\int_\Omega\nabla u\cdot\nabla v+(b\cdot\nabla u)v\,dx=\int_\Omega fv\,dx$ for every $v\in H_0^1(\Omega;\mathbb R)$. The case $b=0$ is the symmetric Laplace model. Given $U\in V(\mathcal T)$, its cell residual is $R_K(U)=f|_K-b\cdot\nabla(U|_K)$; this is $f+\Delta U-b\cdot\nabla U$ because $\Delta U=0$ on each cell. For an interior edge $E=K^+\cap K^-$ define the outward flux jump
$$J_E(U)=\nabla U|_{K^+}\cdot n_{K^+}+\nabla U|_{K^-}\cdot n_{K^-},$$
where $n_{K^\pm}$ are the unit outward normals. Set
$$\eta_K(U)^2=h_K^2\|R_K(U)\|_{L^2(K)}^2+\frac12\sum_{E\subset\partial K,\ E\ {\rm interior}}h_E\|J_E(U)\|_{L^2(E)}^2,$$
and $\eta(U,\mathcal S)^2=\sum_{K\in\mathcal S}\eta_K(U)^2$ for $\mathcal S\subset\mathcal T$. The factor $1/2$ assigns each interior-edge contribution once globally. Let $\Pi_K^0$ be the $L^2(K)$ projection onto constants. The cell data oscillation is
$$\operatorname{osc}_K(U)^2=h_K^2\|R_K(U)-\Pi_K^0R_K(U)\|_{L^2(K)}^2,\qquad \operatorname{osc}(U,\mathcal S)^2=\sum_{K\in\mathcal S}\operatorname{osc}_K(U)^2.$$
Since $b\cdot\nabla U$ is constant on $K$, this oscillation equals $h_K^2\|f-\Pi_K^0f\|_2^2$.

For a separate definitional interface, consider the symmetric diffusion model $-\operatorname{div}(A\nabla u)=f$, where $A$ is a symmetric uniformly elliptic matrix field in the sense of [[def-uniformly-elliptic-divergence-form-operator]] and is Lipschitz on each cell. Its cell residual for a piecewise-affine $U$ is $R_K^A(U)=f+\operatorname{div}(A\nabla U)$, and its outward conormal-flux jump is the sum of $A\nabla U\cdot n_K$ from the two incident cells. Let $\Pi_E^0$ be the $L^2(E)$ projection onto constants. The projected edge term $h_E\|J_E^A-\Pi_E^0J_E^A\|_{L^2(E)}^2$ records nonconstant conormal flux. The reliability, contraction, and complexity results authored here concern $A=I$ only; this extension supplies notation and no coefficient-dependent theorem.

Assume Countable Choice, as in the Sobolev trace and inverse-estimate suppliers.

Let $\mathcal T$ be a conforming shape-regular triangular mesh, let $u\in H_0^1(\Omega)$ solve the model of [[def-afem-p1-residual-estimator-and-data-oscillation]], and let $U\in V(\mathcal T)$ be its exact P1 Galerkin solution. There are constants $C_{\rm rel},C_{\rm eff}$ depending only on the shape bound and $|b|h_{\max}$ such that
$$\|\nabla(u-U)\|_2^2\le C_{\rm rel}\eta(U,\mathcal T)^2,$$
and for every $K\in\mathcal T$,
$$\eta_K(U)^2\le C_{\rm eff}\left(\|\nabla(u-U)\|_{L^2(\omega_K)}^2+ \operatorname{osc}(U,\omega_K)^2\right),$$
where $\omega_K$ is the union of $K$ and its edge neighbors. If $\mathcal T_*\ge\mathcal T$ refines every cell in $M\subset\mathcal T$ by three generations and $U_*$ is the exact fine Galerkin solution, then
$$\eta(U,\ M)^2\le C_{\rm eff}\left(\|\nabla(U_*-U)\|_{L^2(\omega(M))}^2+ \operatorname{osc}(U,\omega(M))^2\right),$$
with $\omega(M)$ the union of edge-neighbor patches of marked cells. All constants are independent of the refinement level.

Assume Countable Choice, as in the zero-boundary Sobolev convention.

Let $\mathcal T_H\le\mathcal T_h$ be nested conforming meshes and let $U_H,U_h$ be exact P1 Galerkin solutions for the constant-convection model of [[def-afem-p1-residual-estimator-and-data-oscillation]]. Write $e_j=u-U_j$ and $d=U_h-U_H$. For $b=0$,
$$\|\nabla e_h\|_2^2=\|\nabla e_H\|_2^2-\|\nabla d\|_2^2.$$
For constant $b$, assume the explicit dual-pickup bound
$$\|e_h\|_{L^2}\le C_D h_0^s\|\nabla e_h\|_{L^2}$$
for the nested sequence, with $s>0$, where $h_0=\max_{K\in\mathcal T_0}\operatorname{diam}K$, and put $\mu=C_Dh_0^s|b|<1$. Then
$$\|\nabla e_h\|_2^2\le(1-\mu)^{-1}\|\nabla e_H\|_2^2-\|\nabla d\|_2^2.$$
The dual-pickup bound is an additional hypothesis. It is not asserted for every polygon or mesh.

Assume Countable Choice, as in the Sobolev interpolation suppliers.

Let $\mathcal T\le\mathcal T_*$ be conforming P1 meshes with exact Galerkin solutions $U,U_*$. Let $\mathcal R=\{K\in\mathcal T:K\text{ is subdivided in }\mathcal T_*\}$ and let $\omega(\mathcal R)$ be the union of the vertex stars of cells in $\mathcal R$. Then
$$\|\nabla(U_*-U)\|_{L^2(\Omega)}^2\le C\sum_{K\in\mathcal R}\eta_K(U)^2,$$
where $C$ depends on shape regularity, $|b|h_{\max}$, and the local interpolant constants.

For two compatible conforming NVB descendants $\mathcal T_1,\mathcal T_2$ of the same initial mesh $\mathcal T_0$, the union of their bisection forests defines a smallest common conforming overlay $\mathcal T_1\oplus\mathcal T_2$ and
$$\#(\mathcal T_1\oplus\mathcal T_2)\le\#\mathcal T_1+\#\mathcal T_2-\#\mathcal T_0.$$

derivations.claim: Let $\mathcal T^+=\mathcal T\oplus\mathcal T_*$ and let $U,U_*,U^+$ be the exact Galerkin solutions. Best approximation on the overlay gives $e_{\mathcal T^+}\le e_{\mathcal T_*}\le\lambda e_\mathcal T$. By [F2], $\|\nabla(U^+-U)\|_2^2=e_\mathcal T^2-e_{\mathcal T^+}^2\ge(1-\lambda^2)e_\mathcal T^2.$ By [F3], this correction square is at most $C_{\rm loc}\eta_\mathcal T(\mathcal R)^2$, where $\mathcal R$ is the set of coarse cells subdivided in $\mathcal T^+$. By [F1], $\eta_\mathcal T^2\le C_{\rm eff}e_\mathcal T^2$. Combining proves $\eta_\mathcal T(\mathcal R)^2\ge\theta_*\eta_\mathcal T^2$. If $e_\mathcal T=0$, then the comparison condition and all indicators are zero and the empty set is Dörfler.

The bulk algorithm sorts nonnegative weights in decreasing order. Among all sets of a fixed size $m$, the first $m$ sorted weights have maximal sum: replacing any omitted larger weight for a selected smaller one cannot decrease the sum, and repeating yields the prefix. Therefore the shortest prefix reaching threshold $\theta_E\eta_\mathcal T^2$ has minimum cardinality among all Dörfler sets. Since $\mathcal R$ is such a set whenever $\theta_E\le\theta_*$, $|M_E|\le|\mathcal R|$. The overlay cardinality bound [F4] gives $|\mathcal R|\le\#\mathcal T^+-\#\mathcal T\le\#\mathcal T_*-\#\mathcal T_0$.

The **Axiom of Countable Choice**, written $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, is the following
statement.

> For every family $(X_n)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ of nonempty sets indexed by
> $\mathbb{N}$ there is a function $f$ with domain $\mathbb{N}$ such that
> $f(n) \in X_n$ for every $n \in \mathbb{N}$.

Equivalently, in the vocabulary of [[def-choice-function]]: every at most
countable family of nonempty sets ([[def-countable]]) has a choice function.

Assume Countable Choice for the $L^2$ and Sobolev conventions of [[def-countable-choice]].

All functions and data are real-valued. Let $\Omega\subset\mathbb R^2$ be a bounded polygon and let $\mathcal T$ be a finite conforming matching triangulation by nondegenerate affine triangles, with maximum shape-regularity constant $\Gamma$. Write $h_K=\operatorname{diam}K$ and $h_E=\operatorname{diam}E$. Let $V(\mathcal T)$ be the continuous, piecewise-affine zero-boundary subspace of [[def-broken-and-conforming-polynomial-spaces]], which lies in $H_0^1(\Omega;\mathbb R)$ by [[thm-matching-continuous-piecewise-polynomials-are-wkp]] and [[thm-zero-boundary-piecewise-polynomials-in-w10p]]. The exact weak model is
$$-\Delta u+b\cdot\nabla u=f,\qquad u\in H_0^1(\Omega;\mathbb R),\quad f\in L^2(\Omega;\mathbb R),\quad b\in\mathbb R^2\ \text{constant}.$$
The weak form is $\int_\Omega\nabla u\cdot\nabla v+(b\cdot\nabla u)v\,dx=\int_\Omega fv\,dx$ for every $v\in H_0^1(\Omega;\mathbb R)$. The case $b=0$ is the symmetric Laplace model. Given $U\in V(\mathcal T)$, its cell residual is $R_K(U)=f|_K-b\cdot\nabla(U|_K)$; this is $f+\Delta U-b\cdot\nabla U$ because $\Delta U=0$ on each cell. For an interior edge $E=K^+\cap K^-$ define the outward flux jump
$$J_E(U)=\nabla U|_{K^+}\cdot n_{K^+}+\nabla U|_{K^-}\cdot n_{K^-},$$
where $n_{K^\pm}$ are the unit outward normals. Set
$$\eta_K(U)^2=h_K^2\|R_K(U)\|_{L^2(K)}^2+\frac12\sum_{E\subset\partial K,\ E\ {\rm interior}}h_E\|J_E(U)\|_{L^2(E)}^2,$$
and $\eta(U,\mathcal S)^2=\sum_{K\in\mathcal S}\eta_K(U)^2$ for $\mathcal S\subset\mathcal T$. The factor $1/2$ assigns each interior-edge contribution once globally. Let $\Pi_K^0$ be the $L^2(K)$ projection onto constants. The cell data oscillation is
$$\operatorname{osc}_K(U)^2=h_K^2\|R_K(U)-\Pi_K^0R_K(U)\|_{L^2(K)}^2,\qquad \operatorname{osc}(U,\mathcal S)^2=\sum_{K\in\mathcal S}\operatorname{osc}_K(U)^2.$$
Since $b\cdot\nabla U$ is constant on $K$, this oscillation equals $h_K^2\|f-\Pi_K^0f\|_2^2$.

For a separate definitional interface, consider the symmetric diffusion model $-\operatorname{div}(A\nabla u)=f$, where $A$ is a symmetric uniformly elliptic matrix field in the sense of [[def-uniformly-elliptic-divergence-form-operator]] and is Lipschitz on each cell. Its cell residual for a piecewise-affine $U$ is $R_K^A(U)=f+\operatorname{div}(A\nabla U)$, and its outward conormal-flux jump is the sum of $A\nabla U\cdot n_K$ from the two incident cells. Let $\Pi_E^0$ be the $L^2(E)$ projection onto constants. The projected edge term $h_E\|J_E^A-\Pi_E^0J_E^A\|_{L^2(E)}^2$ records nonconstant conormal flux. The reliability, contraction, and complexity results authored here concern $A=I$ only; this extension supplies notation and no coefficient-dependent theorem.

For any compatible 2D initial labeling from [[def-afem-nvb-labelled-triangulation-family]], every conforming NVB descendant has shape regularity bounded by a constant depending only on the initial mesh. Three complete generations of uniform bisection of a triangle split each original edge at its midpoint, create a new interior midpoint on the median from the opposite vertex, and give child diameters at most half the parent diameter.

Fix a compatible labeled initial mesh. Recursive reference-edge closure of any finite marked set terminates, produces a matching conforming NVB descendant, and preserves the shape bound of [[lem-afem-nvb-shape-regularity-and-three-generation-properties]]. For a sequence of such refinements in which each selected cell is first requested for three uniform generations, there is a constant $C_{\rm cl}$ depending only on the initial mesh such that
$$\#\mathcal T_n-\#\mathcal T_0\le C_{\rm cl}\sum_{k=0}^{n-1}\#M_k.$$
The constant is for the cumulative sequence; no uniform bound on the added cells in one single refinement call is asserted.

Assume Countable Choice. Fix polynomial degree $k\ge0$, $1\le p,q\le\infty$, and integers
$0\le m\le\ell\le k$. Let the shape-regular affine simplex family be as in
[[def-matching-affine-simplicial-meshes]]. For every cell $K$ in that family,
there is a constant independent of cell size such that, for every
$v\in\mathbb P_k(K)$ and every facet $F\subset\partial K$,
$$|v|_{W^{\ell,p}(K)} \le C h_K^{m-\ell+d(1/p-1/q)}|v|_{W^{m,q}(K)},$$
$$\|v\|_{L^p(F)} \le C h_K^{(d-1)/p-d/q}\|v\|_{L^q(K)}.$$
Use $1/\infty=0$. Constants may depend on $d,k,p,q$ and the family shape
regularity bound, but not on $K$ or $h_K$.

Assume Countable Choice. Let $F_K(\widehat x)=b_K+A_K\widehat x$ map the fixed reference simplex
$\widehat S_d$ bijectively to a cell $K$ of a shape-regular family, and let
$h_K$ be its diameter and $\rho_K$ its inradius. There are constants
$c,C>0$, depending only on $d$, the reference simplex, and the shape
regularity bound, such that
$$c h_K\le s_{\min}(A_K)\le \|A_K\|\le C h_K, \qquad c h_K^d\le\det A_K\le C h_K^d.$$
For each facet $F$, its affine surface Jacobian is comparable to
$h_K^{d-1}$, and its altitude from the opposite vertex is comparable to
$h_K$. Thus Sobolev scaling constants can be expressed using $h_K$ alone,
with constants uniform over the family.

abla u\cdot
abla v+(b\cdot
abla u)v\,dx=\int_\Omega fv\,dx\qquad(v\in H_0^1(\Omega)).$$
No $H^2$ regularity is asserted.

Assume Countable Choice. Let $V$ be a real or complex Hilbert space and let
$a:V\times V\to\mathbb K$ be linear in its first argument, conjugate-linear
in its second, bounded by $M$, and coercive with constant $\alpha>0$:
$$|a(v,w)|\le M\|v\|_V\|w\|_V,\qquad \operatorname{Re}a(v,v)\ge\alpha\|v\|_V^2.$$

statement.

> For every family $(X_n)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ of nonempty sets indexed by
> $\mathbb{N}$ there is a function $f$ with domain $\mathbb{N}$ such that
> $f(n) \in X_n$ for every $n \in \mathbb{N}$.

countable family of nonempty sets ([[def-countable]]) has a choice function.

Assume Countable Choice for the $L^2$ and Sobolev conventions of [[def-countable-choice]].

All functions and data are real-valued. Let $\Omega\subset\mathbb R^2$ be a bounded polygon and let $\mathcal T$ be a finite conforming matching triangulation by nondegenerate affine triangles, with maximum shape-regularity constant $\Gamma$. Write $h_K=\operatorname{diam}K$ and $h_E=\operatorname{diam}E$. Let $V(\mathcal T)$ be the continuous, piecewise-affine zero-boundary subspace of [[def-broken-and-conforming-polynomial-spaces]], which lies in $H_0^1(\Omega;\mathbb R)$ by [[thm-matching-continuous-piecewise-polynomials-are-wkp]] and [[thm-zero-boundary-piecewise-polynomials-in-w10p]]. The exact weak model is
$$-\Delta u+b\cdot\nabla u=f,\qquad u\in H_0^1(\Omega;\mathbb R),\quad f\in L^2(\Omega;\mathbb R),\quad b\in\mathbb R^2\ \text{constant}.$$
The weak form is $\int_\Omega\nabla u\cdot\nabla v+(b\cdot\nabla u)v\,dx=\int_\Omega fv\,dx$ for every $v\in H_0^1(\Omega;\mathbb R)$. The case $b=0$ is the symmetric Laplace model. Given $U\in V(\mathcal T)$, its cell residual is $R_K(U)=f|_K-b\cdot\nabla(U|_K)$; this is $f+\Delta U-b\cdot\nabla U$ because $\Delta U=0$ on each cell. For an interior edge $E=K^+\cap K^-$ define the outward flux jump
$$J_E(U)=\nabla U|_{K^+}\cdot n_{K^+}+\nabla U|_{K^-}\cdot n_{K^-},$$
where $n_{K^\pm}$ are the unit outward normals. Set
$$\eta_K(U)^2=h_K^2\|R_K(U)\|_{L^2(K)}^2+\frac12\sum_{E\subset\partial K,\ E\ {\rm interior}}h_E\|J_E(U)\|_{L^2(E)}^2,$$

The reliability, contraction, and complexity results authored here concern $A=I$ only; this extension supplies notation and no coefficient-dependent theorem.

Let $V(\mathcal T)$ be the continuous, piecewise-affine zero-boundary subspace of [[def-broken-and-conforming-polynomial-spaces]], which lies in $H_0^1(\Omega;\mathbb R)$ by [[thm-matching-continuous-piecewise-polynomials-are-wkp]] and [[thm-zero-boundary-piecewise-polynomials-in-w10p]]. The exact weak model is
$$-\Delta u+b\cdot\nabla u=f,\qquad u\in H_0^1(\Omega;\mathbb R),\quad f\in L^2(\Omega;\mathbb R),\quad b\in\mathbb R^2\ \text{constant}.$$
The weak form is $\int_\Omega\nabla u\cdot\nabla v+(b\cdot\nabla u)v\,dx=\int_\Omega fv\,dx$ for every $v\in H_0^1(\Omega;\mathbb R)$. The case $b=0$ is the symmetric Laplace model. Given $U\in V(\mathcal T)$, its cell residual is $R_K(U)=f|_K-b\cdot\nabla(U|_K)$; this is $f+\Delta U-b\cdot\nabla U$ because $\Delta U=0$ on each cell. For an interior edge $E=K^+\cap K^-$ define the outward flux jump
$$J_E(U)=\nabla U|_{K^+}\cdot n_{K^+}+\nabla U|_{K^-}\cdot n_{K^-},$$
where $n_{K^\pm}$ are the unit outward normals. Set
$$\eta_K(U)^2=h_K^2\|R_K(U)\|_{L^2(K)}^2+\frac12\sum_{E\subset\partial K,\ E\ {\rm interior}}h_E\|J_E(U)\|_{L^2(E)}^2,$$
and $\eta(U,\mathcal S)^2=\sum_{K\in\mathcal S}\eta_K(U)^2$ for $\mathcal S\subset\mathcal T$. The factor $1/2$ assigns each interior-edge contribution once globally. Let $\Pi_K^0$ be the $L^2(K)$ projection onto constants. The cell data oscillation is
$$\operatorname{osc}_K(U)^2=h_K^2\|R_K(U)-\Pi_K^0R_K(U)\|_{L^2(K)}^2,\qquad \operatorname{osc}(U,\mathcal S)^2=\sum_{K\in\mathcal S}\operatorname{osc}_K(U)^2.$$
Since $b\cdot\nabla U$ is constant on $K$, this oscillation equals $h_K^2\|f-\Pi_K^0f\|_2^2$.

For a separate definitional interface, consider the symmetric diffusion model $-\operatorname{div}(A\nabla u)=f$, where $A$ is a symmetric uniformly elliptic matrix field in the sense of [[def-uniformly-elliptic-divergence-form-operator]] and is Lipschitz on each cell. Its cell residual for a piecewise-affine $U$ is $R_K^A(U)=f+\operatorname{div}(A\nabla U)$, and its outward conormal-flux jump is the sum of $A\nabla U\cdot n_K$ from the two incident cells. Let $\Pi_E^0$ be the $L^2(E)$ projection onto constants. The projected edge term $h_E\|J_E^A-\Pi_E^0J_E^A\|_{L^2(E)}^2$ records nonconstant conormal flux. The reliability, contraction, and complexity results authored here concern $A=I$ only; this extension supplies notation and no coefficient-dependent theorem.

For any compatible 2D initial labeling from [[def-afem-nvb-labelled-triangulation-family]], every conforming NVB descendant has shape regularity bounded by a constant depending only on the initial mesh. Three complete generations of uniform bisection of a triangle split each original edge at its midpoint, create a new interior midpoint on the median from the opposite vertex, and give child diameters at most half the parent diameter.

Assume Countable Choice for the $L^2$ projection convention.

Suppose the three-generation marked refinement call completes and returns $\mathcal T_*\ge\mathcal T$, and let $\operatorname{osc}_\mathcal T(K)^2=h_K^2\|f-\Pi_K^0f\|_2^2$. For a Dörfler set $M_O$ with parameter $\theta_O\in(0,1]$,
$$\operatorname{osc}_{\mathcal T_*}^2\le\gamma_O\operatorname{osc}_{\mathcal T}^2,\qquad \gamma_O=1-\frac34\theta_O<1.$$

The region $x+y\le1/2$ is the corner triangle whose other two vertices are the midpoints of the coordinate-axis edges. By [F2] its boundary is a union of refined edges; each refined leaf lies wholly in this region or its complement. Thus $f$ is constant on every child, every child P0 projection is exact, and the refined oscillation is zero. This verifies the strict reduction and agrees with [F3], which gives $\gamma_O=1/4$ at $\theta_O=1$.
